set.body:
Raised by independent review. This is partly a consequence of my own earlier recommendation to pin the tolerances, so the coupling it introduced is worth fixing properly.

WHAT CHANGED

test-crossnobis-known.R now uses replications <- 64L (line 330). It previously used 120. The pinned constants at line 362 were not changed:

  expected_standard_errors <- c(null = 0.0058, signal = 0.0119)

Those values were measured at 120 replications - I supplied them from a base-R replication at that count. Monte Carlo standard error scales as 1/sqrt(replications), so at 64 they should be about sqrt(120/64) = 1.37x larger.

MEASURED, replicating the exact fixture in base R:

  reps= 64   observed se: null 0.00860  signal 0.01418
             pinned   se: null 0.00580  signal 0.01190
             ratio observed/pinned: null 1.48  signal 1.19
             headroom to the 1.5x variance gate: null 1%   signal 26%

The test asserts expect_lte(standard_errors[["null"]], 1.5 * expected_standard_errors[["null"]]). At 1.48 versus a bound of 1.50 that passes with ONE PERCENT of margin. A different seed, BLAS, R version or platform will trip it.

IT IS ALSO WEAKER THAN INTENDED IN THE OTHER DIRECTION

The mean gates are 4 * pinned. Expressed in ACTUAL standard errors at 64 replications, the null gate is now 4/1.48 = 2.7 sigma rather than 4 sigma. So the test simultaneously sits 1% from a spurious variance failure and applies a weaker-than-designed bias gate. Both directions are wrong, from the same cause.

FIX - three options, third preferred

1. Restore replications = 120. The pinned constants are then correct as measured.
2. Keep 64 and rescale: null 0.0079, signal 0.0163 (pinned * sqrt(120/64)).
3. PREFERRED - decouple the constant from the replication count. Pin the per-replication SD instead of the standard error, and derive the gate inside the test:

     expected_sd <- c(null = 0.0635, signal = 0.1304)      # pinned se * sqrt(120)
     expected_se <- expected_sd / sqrt(replications)

   Then changing replications can never invalidate the constants again. That removes the coupling that caused this, rather than patching the symptom.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: Epic 9 will certify on this suite. A gate sitting 1% from spurious failure is a poor thing to certify against, and a 2.7-sigma bias gate is not what the acceptance wording describes.
set.title: Epic 6 MC test: replications cut 120 to 64 but the pinned standard errors were not rescaled (1% headroom)
